src: Contrast-enhanced CT shows a 3 cm hypodense mass in segment VI of the liver with arterial phase hyperenhancement and washout on the portal venous phase, classified as LR-5 according to LI-RADS.
On MRI, the lesion is hyperintense on T2-weighted images and hypointense on T1-weighted images, with restricted diffusion and a low ADC value.
Ultrasound shows a hypoechoic solid nodule with irregular margins, microcalcifications and a taller-than-wide shape (ACR TI-RADS 5).

src: A spiculated mass with heterogeneous enhancement is seen in the right upper lobe.
The patient underwent transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) followed by radiofrequency ablation (RFA); tumour response was assessed with mRECIST.
must_not: cắt đốt bằng tần số vô tuyến

src: According to RECIST 1.1, the sum of diameters of the target lesions decreased by 35%, consistent with a partial response; no new lesions were detected.
Ultrasound-guided percutaneous drainage of the liver abscess was performed with technical success.
This is a Bosniak IIF cystic renal lesion with thin septations and no enhancing solid component.
FDG PET/CT demonstrated a hypermetabolic lesion with an SUVmax of 12, and bone scintigraphy showed multiple bone metastases.
On non-contrast CT the adrenal nodule measured below 10 HU, and the absolute washout on delayed phase imaging was 65%.
The attenuation of the lesion was 45 HU before contrast injection.
A gadolinium-based contrast agent was administered, and the lesion showed rim enhancement on the hepatobiliary phase.
Impression: the findings are suggestive of a malignant lesion; malignancy cannot be excluded and clinical correlation is recommended.
Digital subtraction angiography showed active extravasation from a splenic artery pseudoaneurysm, which was treated with coil embolization.
must: chụp mạch số hóa xóa nền

src: Low-dose CT screening found a part-solid nodule in the left lower lobe, classified as Lung-RADS 4A.
